candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — Continuity of Care, printed p.21 / PDF p.25: perform procedures necessary to safely admit, transfer and/or discharge a client; follow up on unresolved issues regarding client care
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Continuity of Care / postdischarge medication discrepancy follow-up
candidate.educational_objective: During postdischarge follow-up, identify medication discrepancies promptly, coordinate clarification with the appropriate clinical team, and confirm the client's understanding of the corrected medication plan.

options.A: Compare the reported medications with the discharge plan, clarify the discrepancy with the appropriate clinical team, and confirm the corrected instructions with the client
options.B: Tell the client to use whichever medication list is easiest to follow until the next scheduled appointment
options.C: Advise the client to stop all prescribed medications until every discrepancy can be reviewed
options.D: Document the discrepancy but defer further action until the client's next routine office visit

candidate.rationale: AHRQ's Re-Engineered Discharge postdischarge follow-up tool directs clinical staff to review medication lists, identify discrepancies, and resolve inconsistencies by communicating with the hospital team and/or primary care provider as appropriate. During the call, medication problems that require intervention should be referred to the appropriate clinical team, and teach-back is used after discrepancies are resolved to confirm understanding. Choosing an arbitrary list, stopping all medications without an order, or delaying action leaves a potentially unsafe transition-of-care problem unresolved. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A postdischarge follow-up call should identify medication discrepancies, coordinate their resolution with the appropriate clinical team, and verify the client's understanding rather than leave discrepancies unresolved.
candidate.source_document_title: Re-Engineered Discharge (RED) Toolkit — Tool 5: How To Conduct a Postdischarge Followup Phone Call
candidate.source_locator: Sections 'Check Accuracy and Safety of Medicine Lists,' 'Conducting the Phone Call,' and 'Check Medicines': compare medication lists for consistency; resolve discrepancies with the hospital team and/or PCP; problem-solve and refer issues requiring intervention to the appropriate clinical team; after discrepancies are resolved, follow up and use teach-back to confirm understanding
candidate.source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ)

candidate.stem: During a postdischarge follow-up call, a client reports that the medication list being followed at home does not match the medication instructions provided at discharge. What is the nurse's best action?
